label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
**Lee — worth a look at that dumper?**

We’ve known each other 15 years, so I’ll keep this simple: I reckon it’s worth us looking at buying a secondhand dumper together rather than hiring one every time.

We hired the tracked dumper for 14 days this year. At £85 a day, plus £30 delivery each time, it came to roughly **£1,600 all in**. There are already three patio digs and the Boughton drive booked in for spring, so we know we’ll have work for it.

There’s a 2019, 500kg tracked dumper for sale in Faversham at **£1,650 ono**. The seller says it had new tracks fitted last spring. At half each, that’s **£825 apiece**. I can keep it under cover in my lean-to at the yard.

On this year’s use, it could pay for itself in about a year; even at half that use, roughly two years — **before servicing and repairs**. And if it doesn’t suit us, we can sell it on. These machines seem to hold their value, so we’re not necessarily stuck with it.

It’s not just the hire bill, either. In September, the hire place didn’t have one, so we barrowed six tonnes of muck at Hernhill. That cost us two extra days, and your back was gone for a week. Another time the delivery driver turned up at 11 and we lost half the morning. Having our own would mean less waiting around and less shifting by hand.

For costs, I suggest we split routine servicing 50/50. If one of us breaks it through our own use, that person covers the repair. We can agree the details before we buy.

Come and have a look at it with me this Saturday before someone else gets it. No pressure to commit — let’s check it over and see if the sums still stack up.
